sketches.title: Pub Proof
sketches.premise: You are building one conspiracy theory, one clue at a time, while the host reports on your very serious investigation. Start with an ordinary oddity and make it suspicious; your partner must keep the same theory alive without quietly changing what it claims.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds exactly one connected clue that makes the shared theory more believable and fits every stated fact; a skipped link is a jump with no usable connection, an ending is a final claim that leaves no room for another clue, and an undo is denying or replacing a clue already accepted.
sketches.move_shape: Add one clue and its link to the theory: “The pub clock is seven minutes slow, so the council can make every witness arrive late.”
sketches.first_card: The pub clock is seven minutes slow.

sketches.title: Cover-Up Chain
sketches.premise: One tiny pub incident has been covered up by a chain of people, objects, and favors. Take turns naming the next link, with the host offering earnest commentary while your partner gets stuck holding the suspicious bag.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it names exactly one new link that directly passes the secret from the last link to the next and preserves the whole chain; a skipped link leaps over who or what carried it, an ending seals the chain, and an undo removes or changes a link already in it.
sketches.move_shape: Name one next carrier and why: “The cleaner hid the key in the landlord’s biscuit tin.”
sketches.first_card: A muddy key was found behind the pub dartboard.

sketches.title: The Pub Predicted It
sketches.premise: The pub has a conspiracy theory about an event that has not happened yet. Build one shared prediction step by step, making each new detail follow from the clues already on the table; the host treats your nonsense with grave respect.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds exactly one forecastable event that follows from every clue so far and still leaves a next event possible; a skipped link jumps to an outcome without a cause, an ending makes the prediction complete, and an undo cancels or rewrites an earlier forecast.
sketches.move_shape: Add one likely next event: “Because the lights blinked three times, the mayor’s car will stop outside before closing.”
sketches.first_card: Three lights blinked above the pub door.

sketches.title: The Suspicious Map
sketches.premise: Draw a conspiracy across the pub: each turn places one person, object, or meeting in the next connected spot. The theory may be ridiculous, but the route must be clear enough for a stranger to follow—and for your partner to be trapped by it.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds exactly one connected location or thing and preserves one continuous route through all earlier points; a skipped link crosses an unexplained gap, an ending reaches the named secret, and an undo moves or deletes an earlier point.
sketches.move_shape: Add one connected stop: “From the cellar, the envelope went through the kitchen hatch to the coat room.”
sketches.first_card: A locked box sits under the pub stage.

sketches.title: Rumour Receipt
sketches.premise: Invent one pub conspiracy and build its paper trail, one receipt-like record at a time. Every new scrap must explain how it joins the same scheme, while the host reads the evidence as if Parliament might be listening.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds exactly one dated or signed record that supports and connects to the entire existing paper trail; a skipped link gives evidence with no source or connection, an ending proves the scheme, and an undo rejects or alters a record already accepted.
sketches.move_shape: Add one record: “Tuesday, 9:12 p.m.—Nina paid cash for twelve lemons, though the bar sold none.”
sketches.first_card: A receipt for twelve lemons was found in the pub till.

sketches.title: Theory With Teeth
sketches.premise: Build a single conspiracy theory whose clues slowly force an innocent-looking person to explain themselves. Each turn adds one pressure point, and the host gives gentle, earnest commentary while your partner decides how much embarrassing detail to volunteer.
sketches.criterion: A move HOLDS if it adds exactly one new fact that follows from the whole theory and increases pressure without making a new target or claim; a skipped link jumps from clue to blame, an ending names the unavoidable accusation, and an undo backs away from an accepted fact.
sketches.move_shape: Add one pressure point: “Since the same red paint is on the van, the door, and his cuff, he must explain why he visited all three.”
sketches.first_card: Red paint was found on the pub door.
